title: Why generics: List versus ArrayList
hook: ArrayList is a bag of object. List<T> is a bag of T. The difference is compile-time rejection, no boxing of int, and a constructed type the CLR still knows at run time.

sections.heading: The ArrayList failure mode
sections.prose: System.Collections.ArrayList.Add(object) accepts an SQS message id string and an attempt count int in the same list. The int is boxed onto the heap. The reader casts: (int)list[0] throws InvalidCastException if someone inserted a string. Hashtable keys and values are object too. This is the 2002 collections story. You still see it in old samples and in COM-era APIs. In a .NET 10 interview, naming ArrayList without saying “don’t use it” is a miss.

snippets.label: The cast that should never ship
snippets.explanation: List<int> stores ints in the backing array. ArrayList stored a boxed object. The compiler is the entire test suite for the mixed-type bug.

sections.heading: Reification, not erasure
sections.prose: Microsoft’s generics overview contrasts C# with Java templates/erasure and with C++ templates. List<int> and List<string> are different constructed types at run time. You can ask typeof(List<int>).GetGenericArguments(). Reflection, AOT, and the JIT use that. TypeScript generics erase completely; at run time you have arrays. That is why a C# Redis serializer can have a closed generic Get<SessionDto> and still know T in IL, while a TS get<T>() is a comment to tsc.

sections.heading: What you reach for
sections.prose: Daily production: List<T>, Dictionary<TKey, TValue>, HashSet<T>, Queue<T>, Task<T>, Func<T, TResult>. Those are generic types you consume. You write your own when the invariant is yours — a cache client, a Result<T>, a handler pipeline. You do not write GenericList<T> as a linked list in 2026; Microsoft’s own sample says use List<T>.

interviewTakeaways: Generics give compile-time T and avoid boxing value types in collections.
C# generics are reified; Java/TS generics are erased.
ArrayList / Hashtable are legacy object collections.
commonPitfalls: Using List<object> as a quiet ArrayList.
Saying C# generics work like C++ templates (no compile-time codegen per T in source; the JIT/AOT specializes).
Boxing anyway by storing structs as interface types inside the list.

jsTsCorrelations.note: function identity<T>(x: T): T erases. C# identity<T> remains in metadata and can be invoked via reflection with a closed T.
JS arrays are ArrayList-shaped: any value, no T. TypeScript only paints T on top.
